_comment: ★ This file reaches the SYSTEM PROMPT as DATA via scout/context/intent_routing.py -> INTENT_ROUTING_CONTEXT, interpolated in scout/agent.py. A wrong tool name here is invisible to any source search: generate_document_tool sat in this file for weeks as the primary source for 'Create legal document'. Every primary_source and fallback_sources value MUST be a really-registered tool name -- _audit_prompt_tool_contract raises at import otherwise. NOTE: the formatter (build_intent_routing) renders ONLY intent, primary_source, fallback_sources and reasoning from intent_mappings; source/best_for/search_first_when from source_preferences; issue/description/solution from common_gotchas. Every other key, including this one and any keywords array, is dropped at load and never reaches the model.
_comment_no_paths: ★ Do NOT reintroduce a known_locations key, or any other file path, into this file. Until 2026-08-06 the one legal intent here pointed company data at documents/legal/data/ -- a directory that exists but has only a .gitkeep in it, because the product is DB-only: company particulars, directors, members, the People register and trained template metadata are all PostgreSQL tables. A path here does not merely fail to help; it tells the model to go looking in a folder that will always be empty, and it comes back with nothing and says nothing. The three directories that do hold files are documents/legal/templates, documents/legal/output and documents/legal/uploads, and they are reached through the file tools, not through a routing hint. Note that U16 checks advertised directories in scout/knowledge/sources/files.json ONLY -- a path added back here would pass the whole suite silently.

intent_mappings.intent: Create or draft a legal document
intent_mappings.reasoning: Preview first so the user sees the filled draft and the fields still missing, then generate once they approve. Never generate straight from the request.
Only the templates tagged as the new-company setup group apply here. Offering the full template list buries the five that matter.

intent_mappings.intent: Find the right template for a request
intent_mappings.reasoning: Match against trained template metadata. If two or more match closely, ask the user to choose rather than picking one.
Company records live in PostgreSQL, entered from the admin panel or extracted from a DICA filing. They are the authoritative source for company facts.
Read the register. Do not infer a director from a previous document or from an earlier conversation.

intent_mappings.intent: Shareholders or members of a company
intent_mappings.reasoning: Members may be individuals or corporate bodies, and the two are treated differently when signing. Check the type before drafting.
Always present a picker and let the user choose. A signer must never be guessed, and the choice must record the role it was made for.
Maps company data onto the template placeholders and shows what is still unfilled, so only the genuinely missing values get asked for.

intent_mappings.intent: Myanmar corporate-law procedure or drafting practice
intent_mappings.reasoning: Load the relevant playbook before advising on procedure. This is a Myanmar practice; do not reason from any other country's company law.

intent_mappings.intent: Look something up in the knowledge base
intent_mappings.reasoning: Semantic search over trained template and company knowledge. Prefer it over answering from memory.
Every generated document is tracked with the company and template it came from, so an earlier draft can be found rather than regenerated.
This QUEUES an email for the user to approve and send. It does not deliver anything. Tell the user the email is waiting for their approval; you cannot approve it yourself.

intent_mappings.intent: Anything not about Myanmar corporate documents
intent_mappings.reasoning: Out of scope. Say so plainly and offer what this system does handle.

search_first_when: any question about a specific company or person
advising on procedure rather than filling a form
unsure who is entitled to sign something
the answer is in the wording of a specific .docx and not in the database

common_gotchas.issue: This is Myanmar law, not any other jurisdiction
common_gotchas.description: The applicable statute is the Myanmar Companies Law 2017 and the regulator is DICA. No other country's company law, securities regulator or filing regime applies, however familiar it may seem. Reciting a neighbouring jurisdiction's provisions here has already caused real defects in this product.
common_gotchas.solution: Cite a provision only when you can source it to Myanmar law. If you cannot, say so and cite nothing at all -- a borrowed or invented citation is worse than none.

common_gotchas.issue: Company data is in the database, not in files
common_gotchas.description: There is no folder of company data to search. Company particulars, directors, members and the People register are PostgreSQL tables.
common_gotchas.solution: Use the company and register tools. Do not go looking for a data directory.

common_gotchas.issue: DICA extracts do not contain contact details
common_gotchas.description: A DICA filing publishes name, NRC, the company address and business occupation. It never carries a person's phone number, email address or residential address.
common_gotchas.solution: Ask for those. Never infer them, and never copy them from another company's record.

common_gotchas.issue: A corporate shareholder signs through its own board
common_gotchas.description: A consent given by a corporate shareholder is signed by that shareholder company's own directors, not by the directors of the company being incorporated.
common_gotchas.solution: Identify whose board is signing before drafting, and confirm the signer through a picker.

common_gotchas.issue: Fixed numbered slots do not mean fixed party counts
common_gotchas.description: Templates hard-code slots such as shareholder_1 to shareholder_3 and director_1 to director_3. These are template artefacts, not a limit on the real number of parties, and the document expands or shrinks to the actual list at fill time.
common_gotchas.solution: Work from the company's real member and director lists. Do not ask the user to fill a numbered slot that has no corresponding party.

common_gotchas.issue: Some particulars are hand-entered and are often blank
common_gotchas.description: A person's father's name and country of residence are required for Myanmar drafting but are not published in a DICA extract, so they are frequently missing from the register.
common_gotchas.solution: Ask the user for them when a template needs them. A blank here is a missing fact, not a value of zero.

common_gotchas.issue: Never guess a name, a date or a figure
common_gotchas.description: A plausible-looking wrong value in an executed legal document is far more damaging than an unanswered question. This system's worst defects have all been confident substitutions.
common_gotchas.solution: Ask. A clarify card costs the user a click; a wrong director on a filed resolution costs them a correction filing.
